newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao to appeal against being denied bail.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao to appeal against being denied bail.

text.p: A court on Tuesday dismissed a regular bail plea by former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in a forgery case and gave him until November 14 to appeal to a higher court.
Immediately after the hearing, Rao's lawyer R.K. Anand told reporters: "He is appealing against this order in a sessions court today."

Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Prem Kumar also gave former minister K.K. Tewary, one of three other people charged with Rao and who appeared in court on Wednesday, until November 14 to appeal to a higher court.
The Central Bureau of Investigation on September 26 charged the four with involvement in an alleged attempt in 1989 to defame V.P. Singh, a Congress defector who later became prime minister.

The other two accused are Chandraswami, a Hindu guru close to Rao and the guru's assistant Kailash Nath Agarwal, who are both in jail. They have been appearing in the continuing hearings in the case and their bail applications have been repeatedly turned down so far.
If denied bail by a higher court, Rao, who has also been charged in a separate case of bribery, could be arrested and taken into custody, legal experts said.
Rao, the first former or serving prime minister to face criminal charges, was in court for only three minutes. He was impassive and left immediately after his plea was rejected.

In a 36-page written order, Kumar said: "After most careful circumspection, I am of the view that in the larger interest of the state and a fair trial ... the accused persons are not entitled to bail at this stage of the case."
But the order added that in view of a Supreme Court order on October 13, they would remain on anticipatory bail for one week.
"Hereafter, subject to orders of the superior courts the accused persons, Narasimha Rao and K.K. Tewary, shall surrender before the court on or before November 14, 1996," it added.

Rao, who resigned as prime minister after his Congress party was defeated in general elections in April and May, appeared in the court twice last week for bail hearings in the seven-year- old criminal forgery case.
The four are alleged to have forged documents which aimed to show Singh's son held $21 million in a bank account on the Caribbean island of St Kitts.
Rao has not commented publicly on the case, whose charges carry a maximum sentence of seven years in jail.
The Congress Working Committee (CWC), the Congress party's decision- making body, on Monday said all senior party members would have to disclose financial assets.

"Congress president Sitaram Kesri disclosed all his assets at the CWC meeting," spokesman V.N. Gadgil told reporters on Monday. "It was decided that all other members of the the CWC would follow the example soon."
